findings: Discovery is metadata-only and consent-gated: FIND_CELL reports only train.7z paths, sizes, and scan completeness, never payload bytes or other filenames; verify_discovery rejects extra keys, non-/content paths, control characters, and malformed sizes. The mount task leaves the plain drive.mount cell unexecuted for operator browser consent, and a spurious COMPLETE on that task fails closed because the mount cell emits no parseable status JSON.

Archive path handling is sound: archive_path requires a /content/-rooted path ending in /train.7z with no control characters or '..' components; the actual path is recorded separately in packet parameters while the pinned run.py still enforces the exact 99,014,629,647-byte size and MD5 36ae28b9a17f7340b8bbef62b595cb57 before any extraction, so a wrong archive fails closed.

The review gate binds correctly: require_patient_review verifies the original P001 science receipt via verify_receipt, then requires a claude-fable-5 response with verdict APPROVE, scope p001-patient-dispatch, matching reviewed_commit, response-bytes SHA-256 matching the execution record, and current SHA-256 of all nine REVIEW_FILES matching the reviewed hashes; it is enforced at packet build (execution_packet) and again at dispatch time (worker).

Model-visible channels carry no patient data: capture_cell redirects both Python-level streams and OS fds 1/2 into 0600 private logs and emits only a fixed status plus source SHA-256, raising only a fixed generic message on failure. Traced fd handoffs confirm the launcher's DISPATCHED print and the inner acquisition status land in the private launch console log; the only model-visible outputs are the CPU-check JSON, the fixed wrapper status dict, and the fixed poll status enums.

Scientific pins are preserved: cells 3-5 of the pinned notebook execute byte-identical via exec of pinned sources in the detached child, acquisition cell 1 is byte-identical inside the capture wrapper, and only operator-context cell 2 (interactive mount plus placeholder OUTPUT/ARCHIVE/DATA_ROOT) is replaced by params with the identical OUTPUT constant and DATA_ROOT=None, matching the documented authorization; tests assert the pinned cell sources appear verbatim in the child script and that all generated sources compile.

Dispatch is detached and nondestructive: start_new_session=True detaches the child from the MCP cell timeout; a pre-existing job directory or symlink causes refusal rather than deletion or relaunch; FAILED status is written only to a job directory the launcher itself created in this attempt (_p001_owned); child status updates are atomic via os.replace. The string-level try-wrapping of the launch source was checked: single replacement site, no embedded repr collision, valid indentation.

VALIDATED status is gated on the original semantic validator: the child reaches state VALIDATED only after validate_return.verify reproduces the aggregate from private checkpoints under the original decision/review bindings, and the child re-hashes each aggregate file against the validator's manifest before snapshotting into validated_return.json.

Private-return packaging is safe: the zip contains only the validated aggregate bundle files, original console, binding.json/checkpoint_index.json, and checkpoints/predictions/failed_attempts with a symlink refusal; staged patient inputs are excluded (test-asserted) and selected_inputs.json with per-case paths stays on Drive; the zip is operator-transferred and never passes through model tools.

Source readback verification is fail-closed: verify_cell_sources requires includeOutputs=false on every get_cells, binds each run_code_cell to both the inserted code and a post-insertion readback equal to the exact packet source, rejects delete_cell/move_cell and any run-count mismatch, and streams() rejects any remote error output; the execute path additionally requires the exact launch-source SHA-256 in the fixed wrapper status via ast.literal_eval of the sole stream line.

Non-blocking: protocol verification is post-hoc, so a misbehaving worker could act remotely before verify_cell_sources rejects the session; containment rests on the pinned private MCP config with --strict-mcp-config, the mcp__colab-worker__* allowlist with only ToolSearch, and the bounded prompt, consistent with the previously reviewed synthetic architecture; deviations still fail closed locally and the launcher's duplicate refusal bounds re-execution damage.

Non-blocking hardening: require_patient_review compares verdict.get('reviewed_commit') to execution.get('reviewed_commit'), so two absent values would compare equal (None == None); the REVIEW_FILES hash binding still protects, but requiring a non-empty commit string would be stricter. REVIEW_FILES also omits locally imported gate/science dependencies orchestrator/campaign_review.py and orchestrator/campaign.py; remote scientific execution uses only the pinned checkout so science integrity is unaffected, but adding them would tighten the local gate.

Non-blocking liveness: a child that dies before writing RUNNING leaves status STARTING indefinitely, and a worker timeout after a successful launch reports FAILED while the detached child continues; both resolve through poll plus the documented nondestructive relaunch refusal and investigator inspection rather than automatic retries.

Tests were reviewed statically only (not executed, per review constraints): they cover the review-gate refusal, archive-path rejection including phenotype-root and traversal cases, byte-identical scientific sources with compiling generated code, metadata scan never opening payloads or leaking other filenames, private failure capture with fixed status, and success-path validation including staged-input exclusion from the private zip.
